deck.title: Warm & Fuzzies — SUEDE Designathon 2026 pitch draft

design.direction: Warm & Fuzzies paper-and-ink presentation system derived from Cecelia's current brand board
design.signature: One appreciative sentence moves from social ambiguity into a made object, then reaches the room as an optional handoff card.

slides.audience_takeaway: Meet the product identity before the spoken story begins.

visual.composition: Cecelia's firefly and the Warm & Fuzzies wordmark alone on white.

speaker_notes: Timing: 10 seconds.
Pause, introduce the team verbally, then move immediately into the contradiction.

motion.description: Reveal the human-drawn identity once; no ambient loop.

slides.claim: We have never had more ways to talk. So why can one honest sentence still feel hard to send?
slides.audience_takeaway: Recognise the contradiction between communication abundance and emotional expression.

visual.composition: Preserve the current opening: one large contradiction followed by the appreciation sentence.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Let the sentence land before naming the problem.

motion.description: Claim, question and example sentence reveal in that order.

slides.claim: We appreciate our friends. We just struggle to show it.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the problem as an expression barrier rather than a lack of care.

visual.composition: A direct problem statement beside one How Might We question.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Keep the claim bounded by relationship, culture and communication style.

motion.description: Reveal the How Might We only after the problem statement is understood.

slides.claim: So we mapped the ways people already show appreciation.
slides.audience_takeaway: See how comparing existing methods exposed an opportunity between low-ceremony chat and high-logistics physical gestures.

visual.composition: A qualitative x/y field: y is practical cost in time and money; x is perceived meaning and expressive effort. Every position is labelled conceptual.

speaker_notes: Timing: 30 seconds.
Explain that the map was an early design tool: it moved the team from a broad social problem toward the format question.
Do not describe the positions as measured or claim the opportunity is an optimum.

motion.description: Place existing methods first, then reveal the design opportunity.

slides.claim: That map changed our research question.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand that the research focused the project on methods of expression rather than measuring affection.

visual.composition: A left-to-right shift from the initial broad question to the useful methods-and-meaning question.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Name words, time, small acts and keepsakes as research categories, not a validated taxonomy.

motion.description: The first question gives way to the narrower research direction.

slides.claim: Interviews changed our diagnosis: a format problem, not a care problem.
slides.audience_takeaway: Remember the few findings that changed the problem frame rather than the interview mechanics.

visual.composition: Three full-width qualitative findings with no quotes, metrics, interview photos or decorative affinity board.

speaker_notes: Timing: 30 seconds.
Blocked until the exact participant count, method, coding, exceptions and finding wording are supplied.
Do not present the current draft synthesis as a completed evidence record.

motion.description: Reveal one finding at a time in causal order.

slides.claim: The relationship is strong. The window to say it is narrow.
slides.audience_takeaway: See how the working diagnosis becomes a design requirement for one grandmother–granddaughter relationship without reducing either person to a generic persona card.

visual.composition: A relationship line between grandmother and granddaughter showing care, routine and the delayed expression moment.

speaker_notes: Timing: 30 seconds.
Blocked until the team confirms whether this is sourced, composite or illustrative and supplies the exact details.
Do not invent names, ages, quotes or behaviours.

motion.description: Reveal both people, their connection, the friction and then the opportunity.

slides.claim: That changed the product: from writing a message to making something for them.
slides.audience_takeaway: See one material design shift caused by the team's critique and iteration.

visual.composition: Three actual prototype iterations labelled as initial assumption, learning and design response: blank page, material exploration and the authored studio.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Use cause and effect: we started with a message field; expressive materials showed that authorship mattered; the current studio treats the output as an object.
Show only what changed the interaction; do not narrate the full process diary.

motion.description: Move through three actual iterations in order.

slides.claim: Warm & Fuzzies is designed to normalise showing appreciation, not manufacture it.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the product goal and mechanism before seeing the flow.

visual.composition: Product identity, one-sentence mechanism and current Home screen.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Say that the care already exists; the product proposes a repeatable ordinary-day ritual for expressing it.
Call it a working prototype, not a proven social outcome.

motion.description: Reveal the human-drawn identity before the home screen.

slides.claim: The sender makes one object, then gives it away.
slides.audience_takeaway: See how authorship, sealing, carrier choice and private handoff form one finite action.

visual.composition: Four-beat sender flow: make, seal, choose how it travels, give.

speaker_notes: Timing: 35 seconds.
Keep the explanation on the object journey, not editor features.

motion.description: Reveal one product state per spoken verb.

slides.claim: The receiver decides when it begins and how it ends.
slides.audience_takeaway: See receiver agency through arrival, opening and keep, close or remove choices.

visual.composition: Three-beat receiver flow: arrive, open, keep/close/remove.

speaker_notes: Timing: 35 seconds.
State that production privacy, identity and persistence remain unresolved.

motion.description: Reserve the strongest transition for the receiver opening moment.

slides.claim: We wrote something for you, too.
slides.audience_takeaway: Experience the receiver side voluntarily through a real QR/link or the no-device fallback.

visual.composition: A physical-looking handoff card with a clearly labelled placeholder for the verified QR and URL.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Blocked until a deployed receiver URL is tested on a second device and the real QR replaces the placeholder.
Participation must remain optional, private, generic and reply-free.

motion.description: Reveal the card only after the invitation is spoken.

slides.claim: Care was never missing. We designed a new ritual for showing it.
slides.audience_takeaway: Remember the problem, the process conclusion and Warm & Fuzzies' proposed role in one line.

visual.composition: Return to the problem in large type, then close on the firefly and product name.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Do not imply the room interaction proves impact.

motion.description: One line, one answer, one identity lockup.
